title: The Love of Christ Compels Us
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Compelling Nature of Christ's Love
subpoints: The Greek term for 'compels' implies being controlled or pressed by a crowd
This love sustains believers in their calling, even amidst opposition
The Corinthian church context highlights the need for this sustaining power

outline.title: Exegesis of 'One Died for All'
subpoints: Refutation of the idea that Christ died equally for every human
The 'all' refers to all who are elect and come to faith
Believers die to self and live for Christ, not for themselves

outline.title: The Paradox of the Christian Life
subpoints: True life is found in dying to self
Union with Christ in death leads to union in resurrection
Abundant life is a gift from Christ, not a result of self-affirmation

outline.title: Regeneration and Justification
subpoints: Death to self occurs at the moment of regeneration
Regeneration is the work of the Spirit through the Word
It involves conviction of sin, enlightenment, and renewal of the will

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro examines 2 Corinthians 5:14-6:2, focusing on the phrase 'the love of Christ compels us.' He explains that this compulsion is not merely an emotional nudge but a controlling force that directs the believer's life toward God's calling. The pastor addresses the theological nuance of Paul's statement that 'one died for all,' clarifying that this refers to all who are elect and come to faith, rather than a universal atonement for every individual. This understanding leads to the central paradox of the Christian life: believers must die to self in order to truly live, as they are no longer their own but belong to Christ.

The message emphasizes that true life is not found in self-affirmation or therapeutic healing, but in the gospel and the work of Christ. Pastor Lyro draws on several other passages, including Matthew, Romans, and John, to illustrate how union with Christ in His death results in a new, abundant life. He defines regeneration as the work of the Holy Spirit through the Word, which convinces believers of their sin, enlightens their minds, and renews their wills to embrace Christ. This spiritual transformation marks the beginning of a new creation, where old things have passed away and believers are reconciled to God through Jesus Christ.
